title: Checkout p99 latency 9s and 502s at the ingress
symptoms: p99 latency on POST /checkout jumped from 300ms to 9s. Ingress returning 502s. Order conversion dropped 40%.
error_signature: HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms

diagnostic_steps.action: Checked CPU and memory on checkout pods
diagnostic_steps.result: Normal, ruled out resource starvation
Low, database itself was healthy
Active connections pinned at max (20/20), 140 threads waiting

root_cause: The 16:45 deploy added a code path that opened a DB connection in the coupon lookup and never released it on the error branch. The pool leaked until exhausted.
fix: Rolled back the 16:45 deploy. Follow-up patch used try-with-resources in the coupon lookup. Pool size raised from 20 to 40 as a safety margin.

title: Cart and checkout requests timing out, thread pool saturated
symptoms: Checkout API responding slowly, then timing out. Alerts on request queue depth. Started about 10 minutes after the weekly release.
error_signature: Timeout waiting for connection from pool; pool stats: active=20 idle=0 waiting=212

diagnostic_steps.result: Relief for about 4 minutes, then the problem returned

diagnostic_steps.action: Checked for slow queries in pg_stat_activity
diagnostic_steps.result: No long running queries

diagnostic_steps.action: Diffed the release against the previous version
diagnostic_steps.result: New retry wrapper around the payment call holds a connection during retries

root_cause: A new retry wrapper kept a DB transaction open while retrying the payment provider call, so connections were held for up to 20 seconds each.
fix: Rolled back the release. Moved the payment call outside the DB transaction, then re-released. Added a pool saturation alert at 80 percent.

title: Order confirmation emails delayed, API latency climbing
symptoms: Order confirmation API slow, 504s from the gateway. Customers report spinner on the order page.

diagnostic_steps.result: Made it worse, more pods meant more connections and Postgres hit max_connections
Deploy went out 25 minutes before the first alert
Each pod held its full pool of 15 even when idle

root_cause: A new ORM version changed the default so idle connections were never returned to the pool. Scaling out multiplied the problem.
fix: Rolled back the ORM upgrade, then pinned pool_recycle and max_overflow explicitly. Reduced replicas back to 6.

title: Intermittent 500s on checkout after feature flag rollout
symptoms: Roughly 15 percent of checkout requests failing with 500. Started when the new loyalty points flag reached 50 percent of traffic.
error_signature: HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms

diagnostic_steps.result: Loyalty points flag ramped from 10 to 50 percent at 16:30
Errors stopped within 2 minutes
Runs a synchronous lookup that holds a connection for the whole request

root_cause: The loyalty lookup borrowed a connection and held it across a slow external call, exhausting the pool as traffic to the flag increased.
fix: Kept the flag off. Refactored the lookup to release the connection before the external call, then re-ramped the flag.
deploy_related: Flag rollout on a Friday afternoon

title: Search API latency spike and Elasticsearch CPU at 100 percent
symptoms: Search latency went from 80ms to 6s. Elasticsearch cluster CPU pinned. Redis hit ratio dropped to near zero.

diagnostic_steps.result: Green, no unassigned shards
Redis cluster was flushed at 09:12 during a maintenance task
Thousands of identical popular queries all missing cache at once

root_cause: Redis was flushed during maintenance. All keys had the same 10 minute TTL, so everything expired together and every request hit Elasticsearch at once (cache stampede).
fix: Enabled request coalescing on the search cache layer and warmed the top 500 queries. Changed TTLs to a base value plus random jitter of 20 percent.

title: Catalog pages slow after Redis failover
symptoms: Product pages taking 5 to 8 seconds. Database read replica CPU at 95 percent. Cache hit rate collapsed after a Redis failover.
error_signature: cache_miss_rate=0.97 replica_cpu=95 slow query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category_id = ?

diagnostic_steps.result: Overloaded with identical category queries
Primary failed over at 10:58 and the new primary started empty
All catalog keys share a fixed 15 minute TTL with no jitter

root_cause: After the Redis failover the cache was empty and every request went to the read replica at the same time. Fixed TTLs made the recovery wave repeat every 15 minutes.
fix: Temporarily rate limited the catalog endpoints and warmed the cache from a script. Added TTL jitter and single-flight locking for cache fills.

title: Search latency degraded again after cache key format change
symptoms: Search p95 rose to 3s. Cache hit rate fell from 92 percent to 11 percent right after the 14:30 deploy.

diagnostic_steps.result: Elevated load but healthy
Cache key builder now included a request id, so no two requests shared a key

root_cause: A refactor accidentally added a per-request id to the cache key so the cache never hit. Similar load pattern to a stampede, but self inflicted.
fix: Reverted the cache key change and added a unit test asserting key stability. Warmed the cache after revert.

title: Notification emails and push messages delayed by hours
symptoms: Consumer lag on the order-events topic climbing past 400k. No notifications sent since 01:50.
error_signature: org.apache.kafka.common.errors.SerializationException: Error deserializing Avro message for id 7311; consumer group rebalancing repeatedly

diagnostic_steps.result: Lag kept growing, consumers crashed again within seconds
Same offset failing repeatedly, then the group rebalanced

diagnostic_steps.action: Inspected the message at that offset
diagnostic_steps.result: Produced with a schema version that the consumer did not have

root_cause: One message written with an incompatible Avro schema version blocked a partition. The consumer crashed on it, restarted, and reprocessed the same offset forever.
fix: Skipped the poisoned offset manually, then deployed a dead letter queue handler so undeserializable messages are parked instead of blocking. Added schema compatibility checks in CI.

title: Order events consumer stuck, lag growing on partition 3
symptoms: Lag on partition 3 of order-events at 250k while other partitions are healthy. Customers not receiving shipping updates.
error_signature: JsonParseException: Unexpected character at offset 1889231, partition 3; consumer group rebalance loop

diagnostic_steps.result: Only partition 3 was stuck
Exactly one message failing over and over

diagnostic_steps.action: Looked at the producer of that message
diagnostic_steps.result: A partner webhook sent malformed JSON that was passed through unvalidated

root_cause: A malformed payload from a partner webhook was published to Kafka without validation and the consumer had no dead letter handling for parse errors.
fix: Skipped the offset, replayed the affected window after fixing the payload, and added validation at the producer plus a dead letter topic for parse errors.

title: Invoice generation stalled overnight
symptoms: Invoice events not being processed, lag at 90k. Finance noticed missing invoices in the morning.
error_signature: SerializationException at offset 552108; consumer restarted 63 times in 40 minutes

diagnostic_steps.result: Crash looping
One event with a null required field

root_cause: A single event with a null required field crashed the consumer on every retry and blocked the partition.
fix: Skipped the offset, backfilled the invoice manually, and enabled the shared dead letter handler library in billing-service.

title: Payments gateway pods restarting repeatedly
symptoms: Pods OOMKilled every 20 to 30 minutes. Payment success rate dipping during each restart. Memory graph shows a steady climb.
error_signature: OOMKilled exit code 137, container memory limit 2Gi, heap growth ~40MB/min

diagnostic_steps.result: Only delayed the restarts

diagnostic_steps.action: Took a heap dump from a pod before it died
diagnostic_steps.result: Millions of unreleased HTTP client connection objects
HTTP client library upgraded from 4.5 to 5.2

root_cause: The upgraded HTTP client library created a new connection manager per request because of a changed default, leaking connection objects.
fix: Pinned the HTTP client back to 4.5 and shipped a shared client instance in the following release. Added a memory growth alert.
deploy_related: Dependency upgrade earlier in the week

title: Payments gateway OOMKilled again after logging change
symptoms: Restarts every 45 minutes, heap steadily rising. Similar shape to the February incident.
error_signature: OOMKilled exit code 137, heap growth ~25MB/min, top allocation: LogEvent buffers

diagnostic_steps.action: Checked whether the HTTP client was still pinned
diagnostic_steps.result: Yes, pinned, so not the same cause
Large retained set of log event buffers

diagnostic_steps.action: Reviewed the new async log appender config
diagnostic_steps.result: Unbounded queue size

root_cause: A new async logging appender was configured with an unbounded queue. Under load the queue grew without limit and consumed the heap.
fix: Set a bounded queue with a discard policy for debug logs and rolled out the fix. Added a check for unbounded queues in config review.

title: Reporting service pods OOMKilled during month end exports
symptoms: Pods restarting during large CSV exports. Memory spikes to the limit within minutes of an export starting.

diagnostic_steps.result: Monthly export
Loads the full result set into memory before writing the file

root_cause: The export loaded the entire result set into memory instead of streaming it.
fix: Switched to streaming with a cursor and chunked writes. Set a memory limit alert.

title: Widespread 503s across services, login failing
symptoms: Login and token refresh failing everywhere. Downstream services returning 503 upstream connect error.
error_signature: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: current time 2026-03-13T06:03:11Z is after 2026-03-13T06:00:00Z

diagnostic_steps.result: Healthy and running
mTLS handshake failures to auth-service
Internal CA issued cert expired at 06:00 UTC

root_cause: The internal mTLS certificate for auth-service expired. The renewal job had been failing silently for two weeks because of a permissions change.
fix: Manually issued and rotated a new certificate. Fixed the renewal job permissions and added an alert for certificates expiring within 14 days.

title: Partner API calls failing with TLS handshake errors
symptoms: Several partners reported TLS handshake failures against the public API gateway. Internal traffic unaffected.

diagnostic_steps.result: Handshake fails, cert expired
Renewal challenge failing because a DNS record changed

root_cause: The public certificate could not renew because the ACME DNS challenge record was removed during a DNS cleanup.
fix: Restored the DNS challenge record, forced renewal, and added the challenge record to the DNS cleanup allowlist. Alerting now covers all cert-manager certificates.

title: Intermittent DNS resolution failures across services
symptoms: Random name resolution errors, mostly from high traffic services. Retries succeeded.
error_signature: getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN; CoreDNS dropped packets, conntrack table full on node

diagnostic_steps.result: CPU throttled
Table near full on busy nodes

root_cause: CoreDNS was CPU throttled and the node conntrack table filled up under peak load.
fix: Increased CoreDNS replicas and CPU limits, enabled NodeLocal DNSCache, and raised the conntrack limit.

title: Logs missing from dashboards, ingest nodes unhealthy
symptoms: Log ingestion lagging and then dropping. Dashboards empty for the last 40 minutes.

diagnostic_steps.result: 100 percent used on the log volume
Retention job had been paused during a migration

root_cause: The retention cleanup job was paused during a migration and never resumed, so the log volume filled.
fix: Resumed the cleanup job, freed space, and added a disk usage alert at 80 percent.

title: Homepage blank for users on Safari
symptoms: Homepage rendering blank for about 20 percent of users, all on Safari. No backend errors.
error_signature: TypeError: undefined is not a function (evaluating 'arr.at(-1)') in bundle.js

diagnostic_steps.result: All normal
Errors only on older Safari versions
New homepage flag enabled 15 minutes earlier

root_cause: The new homepage code used a JavaScript method unsupported by older Safari and the flag exposed it to all users at once.
fix: Turned the flag off. Added a polyfill and a Safari browser check to the release checklist.
